chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) say: Ten sucklings do not make anything (of kinship) forbidden.
ai.seo_question: How many times must a child be breastfed to establish permanent kinship (mahram) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of radha'ah (breastfeeding kinship), specifying that ten distinct sucklings are required to establish a permanent mahram relationship, a view held by many Shia jurists. It highlights the distinction between mere quantity and the specific legal threshold needed to prohibit marriage, reflecting the detailed jurisprudential discussions in al-Isfabar regarding the conditions of breastfeeding.
